The core insight is that defensive positioning is governed by a geometric duality: the center of the rush line aligns opposite the center of mass of the offensive formation. This creates a foundational spatial relationship that governs how defenders distribute themselves. The supporting halfback's placement is constrained by proximity to this center, ensuring immediate backup. The scrimmage proximity constraint introduces a temporal dimension—defenders must balance closeness to the line with ability to react to sudden movements. These primitives form a coherent system where each element is both a consequence and a condition of the others. Failure modes include misalignment of the rush line center with offensive mass, insufficient support distance leading to gaps, or overcommitment to scrimmage proximity causing coverage failures. The system exhibits robustness under symmetric formations but degrades under asymmetric or unpredictable offensive strategies.
